comment: Items of the WinUI 3 theme (microsoft-ui-xaml, docs/porting/winui-theme.md) that the port does not carry, each with its reason. `document` is a path of microsoft-ui-xaml or "*"; `key` is a resource key, an implicit style as {TargetType}, "*" for every item of the document, or "re:<regular expression>" matched against the whole key; `variant` (optional) limits the waiver to one theme dictionary (Default, Light, HighContrast). Read by scripts/winui-theme/status.py and scripts/winui-theme/convert.py.

waivers.reason: Scaled corner radius values as doubles: FerroUI's CornerRadiusToDoubleConverter has no scale. The one use, the radii of the track rectangles of ScrollBar, is a border whose corner radius is scaled by a CornerRadiusFilterConverter (ScrollBarTrackCornerRadiusConverter in Controls/ScrollBar.xaml); the 8x converters have no use in the theme.

Reveal highlight (RevealBrush, the Reveal styles): deprecated in WinUI 3, where the brushes are plain fallbacks and the Reveal styles are kept for compatibility only; FerroUI has no Reveal lighting. The seven brushes that documents of the theme still name (MenuFlyout, CalendarView, NavigationView) are ported as the plain brushes they are. Two keys of the document are not Reveal resources and are ported: CommandBarMoreButtonMargin and AppBarButtonContentHeight, the last definitions of two values of generic.xaml that the CommandBar and AppBarButton templates name.
Reveal styles (ButtonRevealStyle, ListViewItemRevealStyle, ...): deprecated in WinUI 3 (see the Reveal brushes); the default styles they duplicate are ported.
Reveal focus variants of the NavigationView item presenter: deprecated (Reveal focus), and FerroUI has no NavigationView.
Reveal focus visuals: deprecated in WinUI 3; the port reads UseSystemFocusVisuals="{ThemeResource IsApplicationFocusVisualKindReveal}" (always False) as no focus visual (FocusAdorner = {x:Null}).

DesktopAcrylicBackdrop is a system backdrop of a window or popup (Windows composition), not a brush, and MenuFlyoutSystemBackdrop names it; FerroUI's counterpart is the transparency level of a top level, which an application chooses.
MediaTransportControls: no FerroUI control (no media playback).
MediaTransportControls and MediaPlayerElement: no FerroUI control (no media playback).
Pivot: no FerroUI control; FerroUI's TabControl is ported from TabView.

RadioButtons (the group control): no FerroUI control; FerroUI groups radio buttons by GroupName.

ListViewItemPresenterCheckMode: the check mode of WinUI's ListViewItemPresenter, a type FerroUI does not have.
Switches of the chrome that WinUI's ListViewItemPresenter and CalendarViewBaseItem draw in native code; the FerroUI templates draw that chrome with elements and have no such switch.
Switches of WinUI's ThemeShadow; FerroUI has drop shadows (BoxShadows) but no ThemeShadow.
Input validation of WinUI (IInputValidationControl): removed from WinUI 3 before release and inert; FerroUI's DataValidationErrors is built from the error brushes instead.

The implicit style of ContentPresenter (HorizontalAlignment Left, VerticalAlignment Top): FerroUI's ContentPresenter is not a templated control and has no default control theme; a style of every ContentPresenter would be a global style, which the theme does not have. The templates of the port set the alignments of their presenters, as the templates of WinUI bind them.

NavigationView: no FerroUI control (batch B5). DrawerPage, TabbedPage and the tabs of TabControl at the left and the right are built from its panes and items (Controls/DrawerPage.xaml, Controls/TabbedPage.xaml, Controls/TabItem.xaml); the styles of NavigationView itself, its items, item headers and separators have no control to style.

NavigationView: no FerroUI control (batch B5). The item presenter styles of the left and the top pane are written into the tab themes built from them (Controls/TabItem.xaml for the tabs at the left and the right, TabbedPageTabItemTheme of Controls/TabbedPage.xaml for the top pane); the settings item, the overflow button of the top pane and the search button of the pane have no counterpart in FerroUI's pages.
SplitMenuFlyoutItem (a menu item with a primary and a secondary button): FerroUI's MenuItem has no split mode, so no FerroUI control would use the style (batch B3).
The items of ListPickerFlyoutPresenter (the list of a ListPickerFlyout): FerroUI has no list picker flyout, whose other styles are waived with generic.xaml (batch B3).
A data template of a TreeViewNode (it binds the Content of the node), for applications that show nodes: FerroUI's tree view has no TreeViewNode, its items are the data or TreeViewItems (batch B3).
